LD 792 An Act to Fund Medical Research and Cancer Prevention
Testimony in Support March 27, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Health and Human Services Committee, my name is Lisa Harvey-McPherson RN. I am here today providing testimony on behalf of Northern Light Health and our member organizations speaking in support of this bill. Northern Light Health member organizations include 10 hospitals located in southern, central, eastern and northern Maine, 8 nursing facilities, air and ground ambulance, behavioral health, addiction treatment, pharmacy, primary and specialty care practices and a state-wide home care and hospice program. Ninety three percent of Maine's population lives in the Northern Light Health service area. Northern Light Health is also proud to be one of Maine's largest employers with more than 10,000 employees statewide.
Christine B Foundation services address poverty, cancer and nutrition in Maine working to improve the health and well-being of cancer patients including patients receiving care from Northern Light Health.

At Northern Light Mayo Hospital in Dover Foxcroft the foundation staff serve healthy nutritious food to our cancer patients. There are no barriers, the program is committed to serving our patients with cancer. The foundation provides medically tailored food bags for weekly pick up or when patients can't come to the hospital food is delivered to their home. Patients and our clinical staff report that the program makes a significant difference to our patients by removing the cost of food from the list of financial challenges in this rural economically challenged region of our State.

At the Northern Light EMMC Cancer Center staff from the foundation have a table in the lobby twice per week for our patients. Patients collect a variety of nutritious foods including fresh vegetables to bring home. For patients unable to come to the cancer center location on a regular basis, volunteers with the foundation provide home delivery.

The foundation reports that they have prepared and distributed healthy foods equivalent to 507,000 meals, reaching individuals across Maine, 93% living in poverty, 69% food insecure, and 39% socially isolated.

This bill provides one time funding to the Christine B Foundation to support a research project to evaluate the impact of access to medically tailored groceries and dietician counseling on cancer to patients and their families. The structure of this applied research project is a three-arm randomized control trial. Pending Northern Light Health Institutional Review Board approval, member hospitals are to recruit eligible patients, with foundation and contracted staff performing study interventions,

Testimony of Representative Ambureen Rana in support of
LD 792, An Act to Fund Medical Research and Cancer Prevention
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and distinguished members of the Health and Human Services Committee:

My name is Ambureen Rana, and I represent House District 21 in Bangor. I write to you today in support of LD 792, An Act to Fund Medical Research and Cancer Prevention.

In our state, communities in Washington, Penobscot and Hancock Counties have higher overall cancer incidence rates compared to the rest of Maine. Maine's cancer death rate is significantly higher than the U.S. rate. The 2021 age-adjusted overall cancer mortality rate in Maine is 160.3 per 100,000, compared to the U.S. rate of 146.6.

For years, the Christine B. Foundation has been vital in supporting those navigating cancer care and nutrition in my community. Certain cancers drastically impact one's ability to access, consume and absorb healthy foods. The inability to consume healthy foods could result in malnutrition which, in turn, results in weight loss, muscle wasting and weakened immune function, impacting survival rates. According to the Christine B. Foundation, 50% of patients start treatment not meeting their daily total calorie intake, and 75% do not meet their daily fruit and vegetable intake.

Meeting nutritional needs while managing a cancer diagnosis is difficult on its own, not to mention the financial burden that accompanies this new challenge. Financial hardship, which is common among cancer patients, can lead to forgoing or delays in cancer care, loss of employment and income, debt and even bankruptcy. At the Christine B. Foundation, 93% of patients agree or strongly agree that their cancer diagnosis impacted their financial security.

National findings suggest that cost savings will result from "food as medicine" interventions. The Christine B. Foundation is a trusted Maine nonprofit bringing 70% of the cost of this pilot project to our community. The fiscal note attached to this bill secures the remaining funds. As the legislature considers cost savings, data is required to guide that discussion, which is the reason why this investment matters so deeply.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I urge you to vote in support of LD 792.
